Run via tests/harness/gate.py <this file> (L0+L1; calls tests/harness/coverage_audit.py) and
tests/harness/mutation.py <this file> (L2).
MODULE: frontend/schedule.py -- the PUBLIC named-schedule contract a compiler resolves BEFORE
it lowers a CodeSpec into a record circuit. It is NOT a noise/mechanism model and declares no
physical dynamics: a ScheduleTemplate names its required frontend operations + declares the
record-layout policy (detector / final-readout), and the module ships EXACTLY ONE template
('repeated_memory_v1'). It imports NEITHER torch NOR quimb (dataclasses + the sibling
operation.canonical_operation_name), so EVERY public unit is CPU-PURE and IN-SCOPE for full
L0+L1+L2 -- out_of_scope is therefore {} (the AST reconcile refuses any gpu_bound claim on a
torch-less module -> ZERO out_of_scope).
SEVEN public units (AST reconcile _public_units_in_module: top-level public defs + every public
method of a top-level class INCLUDING the load-bearing __post_init__ dunder):
* ScheduleTemplate.__post_init__    -- canonicalizes name (canonical_schedule_name) + each
required op (canonical_operation_name), rewrites both frozen fields; raises on empty
required_operations / empty detector_policy / empty final_readout_policy; then (name is
ALWAYS 'repeated_memory_v1') cross-checks self.to_manifest() against
repeated_memory_schedule_manifest() and raises on any drift.
* ScheduleTemplate.validate_for     -- forwards required_operations + a 'schedule_template
<name!r>' label to spec.operation_set.require (raises listing the missing ops).
* ScheduleTemplate.to_manifest      -- the EXACT {name, required_operations(list), detector_policy,
final_readout_policy} dict.
* repeated_memory_schedule          -- builds the fixed template from the module constants.
* repeated_memory_schedule_manifest -- the fixed template's manifest dict (constants, RAW).
* canonical_schedule_name           -- str().strip() + the single-name membership guard (raise
on anything but 'repeated_memory_v1'; message carries the ORIGINAL name repr).
* resolve_schedule_template         -- identity on a ScheduleTemplate else canonicalize the
name and return repeated_memory_schedule(); a trailing AssertionError fall-through.
The private module constants _REPEATED_MEMORY_REQUIRED_OPERATIONS / _REPEATED_MEMORY_DETECTOR_POLICY /
_REPEATED_MEMORY_FINAL_READOUT_POLICY are NOT units but ARE mutated (module-level literals): a wrap
makes the builder's constructor raise (op fails canonical_operation_name; or the manifest self-check
mismatches) and a case-swap of the required-op constant ALSO breaks the manifest self-check (see below)
-> every constant-literal mutant is covered by the repeated_memory_schedule()/manifest() pins.
L2 DISCIPLINE (100% coverage != discrimination). The schedule name, three fixed policy strings, the
required-op tuple, every manifest schema + guard message are HARDCODED in the test (deliberately NOT
imported): a mutation of any module constant/literal must make the output stop matching THESE literals
-> the pin fails -> killed. Every raising guard is tripped through a real construction/call route with
the EXACT message via assert_raises_exact (kills the XX-wrap / UPPERCASE case-swap / None message
mutants a substring match leaves surviving): canonical_schedule_name unsupported (+ empty + ORIGINAL
name!r), __post_init__ empty-required / empty-detector / empty-final / manifest-mismatch, and
validate_for missing-op (the 'schedule_template <name!r>' label pinned verbatim).
* NAME + OPERATION canonicalization: a PADDED name + UPPER/mixed op inputs construct successfully
and pin the canonical name (kills the .strip() drop + the 'name' setattr-key wrap: under it the
padded input survives -> assert fails) and the canonical required_operations tuple (kills the
'required_operations' setattr-key wrap: under it the RAW upper names survive -> manifest self-check
mismatch -> constructor raises -> test errors).
* repeated_memory_schedule()/manifest() pins kill every constant mutant: a wrap raises at
construction; a detector/final case-swap survives construction but the field/manifest pin catches
the uppercase value; a required-op case-swap is caught BOTH by the manifest pin (RAW uppercase list)
AND by the constructor raising (the constant is consumed canonicalized through the template but RAW
through the manifest, so the __post_init__ self-check mismatches).
* resolve_schedule_template: identity (is) on a template; the name route returns a template whose
manifest == the fixed literal; the unsupported route raises a ValueError FROM canonical_schedule_name.
CASE-SWAP note (the twin of the D24 'operation' batch, but DIFFERENT outcome). mutmut 3.6.0 emits an
XX-wrap AND an UPPERCASE case-swap per string literal. UNLIKE canonical_operation_name (.strip().lower()
-> an already-canonical caller literal's case-swap is byte-identical after .lower() = a genuine
equivalent, D24's documented 0.86 ceiling), canonical_schedule_name does ONLY .strip() (NO .lower()). So
the 'repeated_memory_v1' case-swap is NOT re-lowered -> it mismatches the membership guard and is
KILLABLE. There is therefore NO canonicalization mask here and NO bar override is needed (kill 0.9697 >
REACHABILITY (PROBE, never ASSERT -- confirmed against mutants/ + the gate coverage output). Two
structurally-dead defensive branches, each a registered COVERAGE exemption (not a mutation gap):
* __post_init__ 'if self.name == "repeated_memory_v1"' is ALWAYS True (line 33 assigned name =
canonical_schedule_name(self.name), which returns only that string or raises) -> the False arc
(skip the manifest self-check) is unreachable [exempt line 46, branch]. The comparison's mutants
divert the always-True path into a skipped check and are killed by the manifest-mismatch test.
* resolve_schedule_template 'if name == "repeated_memory_v1"' is likewise always True -> the
trailing 'raise AssertionError(...)' (line 105) never executes [exempt line 103 branch + line 105
raise]. Mutants that FLIP that comparison (mutmut_1 name=None, mutmut_3 ==->!=, mutmut_4 XX-wrap,
mutmut_5 case-swap) DIVERT control INTO line 105 -> AssertionError instead of a returned template
-> all killed by test_L0_resolve_from_name. The SOLE survivor mutmut_6 mutates line 105's own
argument (raise AssertionError(None)) while leaving line 103 intact -> line 105 stays unreached ->
GENUINE EQUIVALENT (no input can distinguish it; killable-kill-rate = 32/32 = 1.0).
RESULT: gate PASS (7/7 units 100% stmt+branch after exemptions); mutation total=33 killed=32 survived=1
kill_rate=0.9697 PASS (bar 0.90). NO exemptions on any unit body beyond the two dead defensive branches;
NO out_of_scope; NO src edit; NO bar override.

exemptions.reason: The `if self.name == 'repeated_memory_v1'` decision is ALWAYS True: line 33 assigned name = canonical_schedule_name(self.name), which returns only 'repeated_memory_v1' or raises. So the False arc (skip the manifest self-check) is STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE -- a defensive/forward-compat guard for a future second template. The True arc (running the manifest self-consistency check) IS covered on every valid construction, and the comparison's mutants divert the always-True path into a skipped check and are killed by the manifest-mismatch test (NOT a mutation gap).

The `if name == 'repeated_memory_v1'` decision is ALWAYS True: name = canonical_schedule_name(schedule_template) returns only 'repeated_memory_v1' or raises, so the False arc (falling through to the AssertionError) is STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE. The True arc (returning repeated_memory_schedule()) IS covered, and the comparison's mutants divert into the fall-through and are killed by test_L0_resolve_from_name.

The trailing `raise AssertionError(...)` is DEAD CODE: canonical_schedule_name (called on line 102) already rejects every non-'repeated_memory_v1' name with a ValueError, so line 103 is always True and control never reaches this defensive fall-through. Its two f-string mutants never execute (genuine equivalents); the unsupported-name route is covered by test_L0_resolve_unsupported_raises_valueerror (a ValueError from canonical_schedule_name, NOT this AssertionError).
